Liposuction Surgery in Bangalore for Localised Body Contouring

Liposuction removes chosen pockets of subcutaneous fat through small cannulas to refine body shape. It is not a primary weight-loss or obesity treatment. NeoSculpt6 plans each case around fat distribution, skin quality, muscle tone and overall health, since smooth transitions between treated and untreated areas matter as much as fat removal.

Need Help? Call Us · +91 99640 60483

What Is LIPOSUCTION?

Liposuction removes selected subcutaneous fat through small incisions using a suction cannula, often after fluid is introduced to aid anaesthesia and limit bleeding. It can contour the abdomen, flanks, back, thighs, hips, arms, chin and selected chest areas when fat is localised and the skin can adapt reasonably well.

Conventional, power-assisted or ultrasound-assisted methods may be considered in selected cases, but the device does not replace careful marking and controlled fat removal. Liposuction does not remove visceral fat, treat obesity or reliably correct severe skin laxity, and future weight changes can alter the contour.

Decide Which Areas Need Contouring—and Whether the Skin Can Retract

The surgeon reviews the abdomen, flanks, thighs, arms, back, chest, chin or other target areas, along with skin laxity and weight stability. If there is significant loose skin, liposuction alone may make it more noticeable and another procedure may suit better.

The consultation covers conventional or energy-assisted methods where relevant, anaesthesia, compression garments, bruising, swelling and the risk of contour irregularity.

OUR PROCESS

OUR LIPOSUCTION PROCESS

The surgeon examines fat distribution, skin quality, muscle tone, target areas and neighbouring regions, and reviews medical history and weight stability.

Treatment zones are marked with the patient in position, including areas needing tapering, to reduce abrupt edges.

Review covers relevant tests, medicines, supplements, smoking or nicotine use, anaesthesia planning and thrombosis risk, with planned volume and number of areas considered together.

Small access incisions are used to remove fat according to the marked plan, with repeated checks of symmetry and transitions and monitoring of fluid balance.

Instructions cover compression garments, early walking, pain control, incision care and activity, plus expected bruising and swelling and warning signs.

Follow-up monitors bruising, swelling, incision healing and whether early irregularities are swelling or need closer review.

Final review assesses symmetry, transitions, skin retraction and consistency with the original plan once swelling has settled and weight is stable.

WHO CAN BENEFIT FROM LIPOSUCTION?

  • Patients with Localised Stubborn Fat

    Patients near a stable weight may consider it for localised fat that persists despite lifestyle measures, once the consultation confirms a discrete fat pocket rather than generalised weight gain or visceral fat.

  • Patients with Good Skin Elasticity

    Skin with reasonable elasticity adapts more smoothly once fat volume is reduced. If significant laxity is present, another body-contouring procedure may suit better.

  • Patients Seeking Multi-Area Contouring

    Several areas can sometimes be treated in one operation if the combined volume, anaesthesia time and medical risk remain appropriate.

  • Men with Selected Chest or Flank Concerns

    Men with localised flank, abdominal or chest fat may be assessed as part of a proportionate plan; in the chest, glandular tissue or skin excess is also checked. Significant obesity, unstable weight, severe laxity, clotting risk or uncontrolled medical conditions may make liposuction unsuitable.

Liposuction Surgery is planned around anatomy, proportion, safety, recovery and realistic outcome expectations.

Liposuction Surgery Cost and Consultation in Bangalore

Cost depends on the number and size of treatment areas, technique, anaesthesia, facility requirements and whether another surgery is combined.

  1. 01

    Number of Areas

    Treating one small area differs greatly from circumferential contouring of the abdomen, flanks and back, affecting operative time, anaesthesia and garment needs.

  2. 02

    Fat Volume and Complexity

    Larger volumes and revision liposuction need more careful marking, fluid planning and monitoring.

  3. 03

    Technique and Equipment

    Conventional and energy-assisted techniques use different equipment; an assisted method is included only when it suits the case.

  4. 04

    Anaesthesia and Facility

    The written estimate should clarify the surgeon, anaesthesia, facility, compression garment and follow-up components.

FAQs About Liposuction Surgery

No. It is a body-contouring procedure for selected subcutaneous fat deposits and is not intended to replace weight management or treat generalised obesity.

Removed fat cells do not regrow in the same way, but remaining fat cells can enlarge with future weight gain.

Some skin retracts after fat removal, but significant laxity may remain and sometimes needs skin-removal surgery.

Swelling reduces gradually, and contour can keep changing over the following weeks and months as tissues settle.

Compression garments are commonly included in postoperative care; duration depends on the treated areas and the surgeon's recovery plan.

Risks include bleeding, infection, seroma, contour irregularity, asymmetry, skin injury, numbness, blood clots and anaesthesia complications.

The contour is easier to judge as swelling settles, so final assessment is made later in recovery rather than immediately after surgery.
